version.changelog: 1.0.2: honest product wording in cross-links, refreshed links.json and version metadata.

llm.summary: The launcher fits its stated purpose, but misleading advice about Windows script protections warrants review before installation.

dimensions.detail: Local workspace creation and optional provider keys are proportionate. A documented, user-selected custom workspace can be outside the profile, contradicting absolute confinement claims; writes remain limited to setup files and folders.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The FAQ falsely implies scripts cannot pose a Defender risk because they are not binaries. The install guide recommends wildcard unblocking and a recursive fallback without explaining the loss of download-origin checks. Instructions to review scripts and avoid Defender exclusions mitigate, but do not resolve, this misleading guidance.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Setup is user-invoked, and workflows require a menu selection or explicit argument. No unrelated agent directives or background execution appear.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistence consists of disclosed workspace files, installed skills, and a Start Menu shortcut. No administrator escalation, startup entry, service, or scheduled task is present.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Installing three named skills and launching user-selected workflows matches the stated purpose; the bundled code shows no exfiltration or destructive actions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Verify the source and review each script before running it. Unblock only individually reviewed files and avoid the recursive fallback: unblocking removes origin markings and can permit unsigned downloaded scripts under RemoteSigned ([Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.utility/unblock-file?view=powershell-5.1)). Keep Defender enabled and respect organizational policies. Review the three separately installed skills before using their workflows.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: SkillSpector advisory downgraded: environment use supports workspace discovery and documented optional provider configuration. Missing tool declarations alone do not establish excessive authority.
[SQP-2] unexpected: SkillSpector's concern is supported by the FAQ's false security reassurance and the install guide's wildcard and recursive unblocking advice. Unblocking can serve installation, but this presentation understates its security consequences.
[SDI-4] expected: SkillSpector advisory downgraded to a documentation inconsistency: the install guide explicitly demonstrates an outside-profile workspace selected by the user; the script does not independently choose unrelated locations.
